independent_variables.name: PART

Across 20 settings, the weight on the selected target increases while the error-term weight decreases, generating approximately 0%–95% correlations. The source does not give the exact coefficients or full formula; the volatility-window statements conflict.

estimation_procedure.description: For each of three induced-correlation targets (logTA, σCFO, σREV), PART is generated at 20 increasing target-weight settings; 250 random samples of 1,000 observations are regressed per setting. The plotted quantity is the fraction of one-tailed PART t-tests rejecting at 5% or 1%, not a regression outcome. The univariate line is omitted because the full standard-control specification is the retained full version.

review_notes: Source-first scope selects the Monte Carlo regressions in Figures 1–4 as the principal family: the paper’s central empirical question concerns size/operating-volatility bias in unsigned-discretionary-accrual tests and the two remedial approaches. The retained specifications include the full standard controls, the full expanded control variants, and the transformed-accrual comparison; univariate nested lines are omitted. AMJT and APMJ are retained as parallel central outcome proxies. The Section 5 equity-compensation model is an expressly final replication/application and is excluded from the principal family.

The supplied reading JSON OCR truncates figure captions on pages 21–22 and 26–27. Those physical PDF pages were visually inspected to confirm the figure outcomes/panel targets and plotted line categories; the reading-backed definitions remain quoted from Appendix B (page 36).

The operating-volatility timing is genuinely inconsistent: the printed Table 1 note says current year plus prior four years, while Appendix B gives t−5 to t. The supplied OCR drops the words “current and” on page 12; I verified the Table 1 line visually. This remains unresolved for σCFO and σREV; the distinct WLS scalar is explicitly t−5 through t−1.
results_review_notes: Table 1 reports descriptive distributions for the empirical source sample; Monte Carlo results use repeated samples of 1,000 observations, so these descriptive groups have a different sample relation.

No descriptive summary is reported for constructed PART or for the transformed WLS outcome versions; Table 1 AMJT/APMJ summaries are linked only to the non-transformation outcome specifications.
